close_reason: Added INVARIANT comment documenting the nc_constrained_types never-cleared semantics
description: nc_constrained_types is set with |= (ORed, never cleared). If a CA adds a permittedSubtrees entry for DNS, then the intersection narrows it to empty (two conflicting DNS constraints from two CAs), the type stays constrained but nc_permitted may contain no DNS entries. The enforcement in check_names checks type_constrained() — which is true — and then requires at least one match in nc_permitted. With zero DNS entries in nc_permitted, every DNS SAN fails. This is the CORRECT RFC 5280 behavior (conflicting permitted subtrees should block all names of that type). The bitmask design is intentional. However this is a subtle invariant: the correctness relies on nc_constrained_types never losing bits, and nc_permitted correctly encoding the empty set for that type by containing zero entries of that type. This invariant is not documented. A future contributor who 'cleans up' nc_constrained_types based on nc_permitted content will silently break the empty-intersection case. Document explicitly.
title: nc_constrained_types bitmask: once a type is constrained it can never be unconstrained
